unit_title: The Core Idea: Action Comes First

before.unit_title: The Core Idea: Action Comes First
before.core_rule: In Celan, what is happening arrives before who is doing it. The language centers the action itself.
before.why_it_matters: This gives the learner the mental shift they need before reading or building any sentence.
before.example_1_english: The action arrives before the actor: I go to the water.
before.example_2_english: The event is framed before the people inside it: I love you.

before.core_rule: A standard Celan sentence begins with the verb, followed by the subject, and then the object or destination.
before.why_it_matters: This is the baseline sentence skeleton. Many later rules depend on this order feeling natural.

after.core_rule: A standard Celan sentence begins with the verb, followed by the subject and then the object or destination. With var, a destination may be bare or explicitly marked with an.
after.why_it_matters: This is the baseline sentence skeleton. Many later rules depend on this order feeling natural.
after.example_2_english: I go to the water (explicit destination).

before.core_rule: Questions place ra at the front of the sentence. Commands place va at the front of the sentence.
before.why_it_matters: These signposts frame the sentence immediately, so the listener knows whether they are hearing a question or an instruction before the action unfolds.

after.core_rule: Questions place ra at the front of the sentence. Commands place va at the front of the sentence.
after.why_it_matters: These signposts frame the sentence immediately, so the listener knows whether they are hearing a question or an instruction before the action unfolds.

before.core_rule: To negate a sentence, place ver directly before the verb. In a negative question, ver sits between ra and the verb.
before.why_it_matters: This shows how Celan handles refusal, absence, and contradiction without changing the overall sentence shape.
before.example_1_english: I do not go to the water.

after.core_rule: To negate a sentence, place ver directly before the verb. In a negative question, ver sits between ra and the verb.
after.why_it_matters: This shows how Celan handles refusal, absence, and contradiction without changing the overall sentence shape.
after.example_1_english: I do not go to the water.

before.core_rule: Use rath to introduce an if-clause. The rest of the sentence then carries the condition through normal Celan structure.
before.why_it_matters: This lets the learner move beyond direct statements into hypothetical, dependent, and contingent thought.
before.example_1_celan: Rath var ser, nor-var I dren.
before.example_1_english: If the friend goes, I will go to the water.
before.example_2_celan: Rath Ya var dren, nor-var I shena.
before.example_2_english: If you go to the water, I will bring coinage.

after.core_rule: Use rath to introduce an if-clause. The rest of the sentence then carries the condition through normal Celan structure.

after.example_1_celan: rath var ser, nor-var I dren.
after.example_1_english: If the friend goes, I will go to the water.
after.example_2_celan: rath var Ya dren, nor-var I dren.
after.example_2_english: If you go to the water, I will go to the water.

before.core_rule: Celan distinguishes speaker, listener, and others through a compact pronoun system, with singular and plural forms.
before.why_it_matters: This gives the learner the people-markers needed to place action and relation clearly inside a sentence.
before.related_terms: I; Ya; La; Ilin; Yalin; Lalin

before.core_rule: Prepositions do major structural work in Celan. They mark direction, accompaniment, origin, absence, elevation, and position.
before.why_it_matters: This helps the learner understand how relation is built in clauses without depending on heavy case marking.
before.related_terms: Var; Ser; Thal; Ka; An; Nor; Esh; Morl

unit_title: Space and Time: An and Nor

before.unit_title: Space and Time: An and Nor
before.core_rule: -al remains the universal continuous suffix. Varan is the lexicalized locative-stative form Var + An: to reside, stay, or be located at a physical place. It does not establish continuous -an. An supplies physical location; Nor supplies time.
before.why_it_matters: This keeps Celan from blurring place and time into one small English-style preposition.
before.example_2_english: I will go to the city.

before.core_rule: Celan often frames identity through essence and embodied quality rather than through rigid fixed labels alone.
before.why_it_matters: This helps the learner understand why identity language in Celan feels fluid, descriptive, and rooted in qualities rather than only categories.
before.example_1_english: The neutral person brings strength and balance.
before.example_2_english: A woman embodying neutrality and balance.

unit_title: Gendered and Neutral Terms in Use

before.unit_title: Gendered and Neutral Terms in Use
before.core_rule: Gendered and neutral language in Celan is relational, poetic, and context-sensitive. The same term can shift in force depending on use and setting.
before.why_it_matters: This helps the learner avoid reading these terms as rigid biological labels when the language treats them more dynamically.
before.example_1_english: My neutral companion flows with the water.
before.example_2_english: A feminine man / a man shaped by feminine qualities.

after.unit_title: Gendered and Neutral Terms in Use

after.example_2_english: The feminine man rests on the seat.

before.core_rule: Respect is built into the words themselves through honorific particles, titles, and elevated forms rather than left only to tone of voice.
before.why_it_matters: This matters because Celan makes social respect grammatical and visible.
before.example_1_english: I go to the water, respected friend.
before.example_2_english: Honored guardian, do we proceed to the city's exchange now?

after.core_rule: Respect is built into the words themselves through honorific particles, titles, and elevated forms rather than left only to tone of voice.
after.why_it_matters: This matters because Celan makes social respect grammatical and visible.
after.example_1_english: I go to the water, respected friend.
after.example_2_celan: aen I var Li-Seren-en an Varthas.
after.example_2_english: I speak to the honored guardian in the city.

before.core_rule: Social language shifts by culture, setting, and register. Different nations or contexts prefer different tones, titles, and metaphors.
before.why_it_matters: This helps the learner understand that social meaning in Celan is not one flat universal register.
before.example_2_english: I go to the water, respected friend.

after.example_1_english: You speak of the future, friend.
after.example_2_english: I go to the water, respected friend.
